title: TCL TV will not power on
shortDescription: TV unresponsive with no standby light.
fullDescription:
TCL TVs occasionally fail to power due to PSU capacitor failures or main board issues. Roku-based TCL models can also get stuck if the system partition corrupts.

Google TV TCL models (Q-series) can be USB-recovered via TCL support.

fixSteps.title: Capacitor inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Open back, check PSU caps for bulging.

affectedModels: TCL S/4/5/6 series Roku, Q-series Google TV
videoSearchQuery: TCL TV won't turn on fix

faq.a: Yes within warranty period; usually 1 year, longer on premium series.

title: TCL Roku TV interface unresponsive
fullDescription:
TCL Roku TVs can freeze due to memory pressure or app conflicts. Roku's restart command (5x Home, 1x Up, 2x Rewind, 2x FF) reliably reboots without unplugging.

Factory reset rebuilds the system if soft reset doesn't help.

faq.a: Factory reset removes channels and account; you'll re-set up Roku account.

title: TCL Google TV freezes or won't load
shortDescription: Google TV interface stuck on splash or blank.
fullDescription:
TCL Q-series Google TV models occasionally freeze due to recommendations engine load or app updates. Clearing cache and a power cycle resolves most cases.

For persistent issues, signing out of Google account and back in helps.

fixSteps.title: Clear cache
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Apps > Google TV Home > Clear cache.

fixSteps.title: Switch to Apps-only mode
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Accounts - sign out to use Apps-only mode.

faq.a: Strips recommendation engine and shows just app icons - faster on lower-end hardware.

title: HDMI input shows no signal
shortDescription: TV not detecting source on HDMI.
fullDescription:
TCL TVs show 'No Signal' when source is off, cable is loose, or wrong input is selected. Some 6-series have known PS5 4K/120 handshake issues fixed by recent firmware.

For TCL Q-series Mini-LED, HDMI 2.1 features need certified Ultra High Speed cables.

fixSteps.title: Switch input
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle inputs and verify source is on.

faq.a: Yes on Q-series and 6-series Roku models with HDMI 2.1.

title: Netflix won't load on TCL TV
shortDescription: Netflix app fails to start or crashes.
fullDescription:
Netflix issues on TCL TVs (both Roku and Google TV) usually trace to network or stored data corruption. The fix differs slightly:

- Roku: Remove and re-add Netflix channel.
- Google TV: Clear app data, then sign in.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall Netflix
fixSteps.instruction: Roku: Remove channel, re-add. Google TV: Apps > Netflix > Uninstall, reinstall.

faq.a: Yes on both Roku and Google TV TCL models - it can be reinstalled.

title: TCL TV no audio output
fullDescription:
TCL audio issues are usually settings-related: output set to external, Atmos passthrough enabled, or PCM/Dolby format mismatch.

Dolby Atmos passthrough conflicts are particularly common on Roku models with non-Atmos soundbars.

faq.a: If TV outputs Atmos to non-Atmos soundbar, audio drops - use PCM/Stereo.

title: Software update did not install
fullDescription:
TCL update failures usually trace to network instability or insufficient storage. Roku models retry automatically; Google TV models prompt you.

Wired Ethernet usually fixes intermittent download failures.

fixSteps.title: Free storage
fixSteps.instruction: Google TV: uninstall unused apps. Roku: rarely needed.

faq.a: Some Google TV models support USB recovery via TCL support; not standard for Roku.

title: T-Link HDMI-CEC failure
shortDescription: Devices don't respond to CEC commands.
fullDescription: T-Link is TCL's HDMI-CEC implementation on Google TV models; Roku models call it '1-Touch Play'. Failures are usually due to the feature being off after an update, or partner CEC disabled.

fixSteps.title: Enable T-Link / 1-Touch
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > System > Inputs > T-Link / 1-Touch Play ON.

fixSteps.title: Enable partner CEC
fixSteps.instruction: Anynet+ Samsung, Bravia Sync Sony, etc.

title: Vertical lines on screen
fullDescription:
Vertical lines on TCL TVs almost always indicate T-CON or panel failure. More common on older 4 and 5 series after 3-5 years.

Reseating ribbons sometimes resolves; replacement otherwise.
whenToCallPro: If reseating fails and not comfortable.

faq.a: Often not on smaller sets - get a quote first.

title: Black screen with audio
fullDescription:
Backlight failures on TCL LCDs (especially older 4-series) cause black screen with working audio. The flashlight test confirms; LED strip replacement is the fix.

Q-series Mini-LED has thousands of zones and individual zone failures can occur but are less catastrophic.

fixSteps.title: Flashlight test
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm panel works under bright light.

faq.a: Often not - replacement is similar in cost.

title: Roku Channel ROKU CHANNEL 009
shortDescription: Roku Channel app shows error ROKU CHANNEL 009 on TCL TV, usually network-related.
fullDescription: Error ROKU CHANNEL 009 indicates a network problem between the Roku Channel app and its servers. Most cases clear with a sign-out, app reload, or network reset. Persistent errors may need firmware update or factory reset.

causes.cause: Stale app cache or expired session token
Outdated TV firmware or app version

symptoms: Roku Channel won't load or play

fixSteps.title: Restart TV
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug TV for 60 seconds then power back on to clear memory.

fixSteps.title: Sign out and back in
fixSteps.instruction: Open Roku Channel, sign out, then sign back in to refresh the session token.

fixSteps.title: Check network
fixSteps.instruction: Run network test in TV settings; reboot router if speeds are low.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Support > Software Update; install any pending update.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall app
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the Roku Channel app from the home screen and reinstall from the store.

whenToCallPro: Only if errors persist after factory reset.

faq.q: Is ROKU CHANNEL 009 a TV hardware fault?
faq.a: No — it is an app/network error and clears with sign-out, reinstall, or firmware update.

title: HDR flicker on Mini-LED
shortDescription: HDMI handshake/HDCP failure on TCL TV; set HDMI Mode to 2.0 or update firmware.
fullDescription: HDMI HDR FLICKER indicates the TV failed to negotiate HDCP/EDID with the connected source. Common with 4K/120 Hz, eARC receivers, and long passive cables. Cycle power on both devices and try a certified Premium High Speed HDMI 2.1 cable.

causes.cause: HDCP handshake failure between source and TV
Source set to output unsupported format (4K120, Dolby Vision)
eARC/CEC conflict with AVR in chain

symptoms: Black screen with audio or no signal

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle the chain
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug TV, source, and AVR for 2 minutes; plug TV in first, then source.

fixSteps.title: Swap HDMI cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use a certified Ultra High Speed HDMI 2.1 cable under 2m.

fixSteps.title: Try a different HDMI port
fixSteps.instruction: Move source to another HDMI input; label the port for 4K/120 if needed.

fixSteps.title: Match source output
fixSteps.instruction: Set the source to 4K60 RGB to test, then raise resolution/refresh.

fixSteps.title: Toggle Enhanced Format
fixSteps.instruction: TV settings > External Inputs > HDMI Signal Format > Enhanced.

whenToCallPro: Replace HDMI board if multiple ports fail with a known-good cable.

faq.a: For 4K120/VRR/eARC, only certified Ultra High Speed HDMI 2.1 cables reliably pass the handshake.

title: Google TV Launcher Restart Loop
shortDescription: Home screen restarts every few seconds.
fullDescription: Crash loop is usually an Assistant or recommendations service that misbehaves after a partial update. Clearing Launcher data fixes it.

fixSteps.title: Clear Launcher data
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Apps > See all apps > Android TV Home > Clear data.

faq.q: What causes GOOGLE TV LAUNCHER CRASH?
faq.a: Home screen restarts every few seconds.
